article.articleHeadline: Do you think the plague is a thing of history? It is still among us and still deadly.
article.articleSummary: Plague remains a global health concern despite its association with the Black Death. Today it persists in Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and, occasionally, the western United States, with pneumonic plague posing the highest risk due to human-to-human airborne transmission. Infections come from fleas and rodents, with bubonic plague causing swollen lymph nodes and severe pain, septicemic plague in the bloodstream, and pneumonic plague rapidly fatal if untreated—often within 48 hours for pulmonary cases. Between 2010 and 2015, roughly 3,000 worldwide cases and over 500 deaths were recorded, with Madagascar reporting the most annual cases; the last major outbreak occurred in 2017. Europe has been nearly free of plague since 1945, though travellers could reintroduce cases. Early diagnosis is crucial, as symptoms mimic flu; delays in antibiotic delivery in remote Madagascar areas remain a concern. A misdiagnosis example in Oregon underscores the need for vigilance.

triage.triage_reason: 無料配布されるべき蚊帳の不正転売という行政・ガバナンス問題であり、疾病の異常な発生や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す情報はないため見送りと判断する。
triage.notes: 記事はマラリア自体の発生状況ではなく、予防用蚊帳の横流し・不正販売という汚職・流通管理の問題を扱っている。マラリアはこの地域で既知の風土病であり、新規性・異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri – Haut-Uélé: Jean Bakomito in Bunia to build a joint response to Ebola and insecurity - LePotentiel
article.articleSummary: Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ituri and Haut-Uele provinces are coordinating a joint response to the ongoing Ebola epidemic and regional insecurity. Governor Jean Bakomito Gambu of Haut-Uele, on 7 August 2026, visited Bunia, Ituri’s capital, to strengthen inter-provincial coordination on security and health. The current epidemiologic situation is a centerpiece of talks, with Ebola affecting both provinces, prompting shared surveillance, prevention, and case management efforts. Beyond public health, discussions address security in eastern DRC and harmonizing strategies against armed groups operating in the region, notably the ADF. The initiative signals a move to transcend administrative boundaries and implement a unified approach to armed violence and health emergencies, aligning provincial actions for the needs of the populations.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ・オートウエレ：ジャン・バコミト氏、エボラ出血熱と治安悪化への共同対応構築のためブニアを訪問
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国のイトゥリ州・オートウエレ州にまたがるエボラ出血熱の継続的流行が確認されており、複数州にまたがる感染拡大と治安不安による対応の困難さから、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と管理可能性の懸念がある。
triage.notes: エボラ出血熱がイトゥリ州とオートウエレ州の両州にまたがって流行しており、地域の武装勢力（ADF）による治安悪化がサーベイランスや対応活動を困難にしている可能性がある。既知の継続的流行であるため「異常/予想外」はNoとしたが、複数州にわたる拡大と治安要因による管理困難性からPICKUPと判断。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Haut-Uele: Economic operators urged to respect barrier measures - ACP
article.articleSummary: Isiro, Haut-Uele, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo – On 7 August 2026, the Federation of Enterprises of Congo (FEC), Haut-Uele group, urged economic operators to strictly observe barrier measures to curb Ebola. Transport sectors should reduce bus occupancy and limit motorcycle riders to two; hotels must disinfect rooms and equipment for each use; pharmacies and shops should provide handwashing facilities and use disinfectants, especially after handling money. Businesses should install handwashing at entry/exit points of restaurants and bars and suspend large gatherings temporarily. Authorities were urged to strengthen border controls with thermo-flash thermal scanners and other preventive equipment. The FEC leader warned that Ebola has claimed lives in the province and can affect anyone without protection.

triage.headline_ja: オー＝ウエレ州でのエボラ出血熱：経済関係者にバリア対策の遵守を要請 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国オー＝ウエレ州でエボラ出血熱による死者が発生し、経済団体が予防対策強化を呼びかけるとともに、国境での検疫強化も要請されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事は経済団体（FEC）による予防措置の呼びかけが主題であり、感染者数・死亡者数などの疫学的詳細は記載されていないため、フルリスク評価では公式発表（WHO/DRC保健省）による確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 'Deeply concerning': WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom warns conflict and hunger are slowing the fight against Ebola
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remain hard to control as the conflict zone hampers containment, according to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. In an exclusive interview with O GLOBO in Rio (2026-08-07), he warns that war and hunger slow the global response. Tedros emphasizes advancing financial reform and finishing the annex to the Pandemic Agreement (PABS), which would enable rapid pathogen information sharing and fair access to medicines and vaccines; the annex is needed for ratification of the broader agreement. He notes the United States’ withdrawal from WHO but expects its return. For Brazil, he highlights three roles: showcasing the SUS health system as a model, Fiocruz’s local vaccine production to address equity, and helping conclude the pandemic framework while Brazil chairs negotiations on the agreement. He also references his prior collaboration with Fiocruz during his tenure as Health Minister.

triage.headline_ja: 『非常に憂慮すべき事態』：WHOテドロス事務局長、紛争と飢餓がエボラ対策の妨げになっていると警告
triage.triage_reason: WHO事務局長がDRCにおけるエボラ流行が紛争により制御困難であると公式に警告しており、重症度・持続的曝露・流行しやすさ・国際支援の必要性など複数のWPRO基準に該当し、社会的・政治的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事はWHO事務局長へのインタビューで、リオデジャネイロは取材場所に過ぎずブラジルでの発生を示すものではない。米国もWHO脱退に関する言及のみで疾病発生地ではないため、いずれも対象国リストから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Almost all beds for potentially infected patients in the city are already full.
article.articleSummary: In Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo, beds for potentially infected patients are nearly full as Ebola activity rises in the surrounding health regions; last week seven people tested positive in Beni. Construction of the Ebola center is hampered by heavy storms that turn the site into a mud pit, threatening the opening timeline. Médecins Sans Frontières supports the center with medications and materials for both Ebola care and regular health services, while International Medical Corps also assists; nonetheless more people are dying from malaria and obstetric complications than from Ebola. A makeshift team—doctor Marius, Ahmed the pharmacist, and six day workers from Beni—has built the center’s pharmacy amid the chaos, with daily queues at the gate for work. The site is advancing a planned ambulance entrance and latrines, and twenty women still attend prenatal care clients, underscoring ongoing healthcare needs alongside the Ebola response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国べニ市で感染疑い患者用のベッドがほぼ満床に
triage.triage_reason: DRCベニでエボラ感染例が増加し病床が逼迫、複数のIHR基準（深刻な影響・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ対応の医療体制逼迫と、マラリア・産科合併症による死亡がエボラより多い点を強調。国際機関（MSF、IMC）が支援中であり、外部支援の必要性が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: DRC: a thesis recommends environmental surveillance to prevent schistosomiasis - ACP.
article.articleSummary: DRC focuses on schistosomiasis prevention; Kinshasa ACP reports a thesis recommending environmental and animal surveillance to curb transmission, especially around Kimpese. Dr. Germain Kapour warns of hybrids forming between animal- and human-infecting Schistosoma, underscoring a One Health approach that links environmental and animal monitoring. Schistosomiasis is a neglected tropical parasite transmitted via water containing small snails; human symptoms include hematuria and abdominal pain, with infertility cited as a potential complication in women. The study details molecular and phylogenetic identification of snails and mapping of high-risk areas to guide vector control. WHO recommends four pillars: annual treatment in affected areas, access to potable water, hygiene education, and mollusc-control; open-air toilets can contaminate rainwater that becomes drinking water. Institutions include INOHA, with acknowledgment of Professors Muyembe and Bompangue.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：論文がシストソーマ症予防のための環境監視を推奨
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は学術論文の紹介であり、実際の症例急増やアウトブレイクの報告ではないため、緊急性のあるシグナルとは判断されない。
triage.notes: 記事は学術研究（論文）の紹介であり、具体的な症例数増加や新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。既知の風土病（住血吸虫症）に対する予防策提言であり、継続監視の必要性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Kasai-Oriental: 54 tuberculosis cases reported at Mbuji-Mayi Central Prison - ACP.
article.articleSummary: On 7 August 2026, Mbujimayi Central Prison in Kasai-Oriental Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, reported 54 tuberculosis cases, with 52 among inmates and none among staff. Director Marguerite Mbelu cited crowded conditions and close proximity, complicating isolation and prolonging TB screening. The facility has TB drugs but malaria medicines are in very short supply, and other medicines are unavailable. It awaits replenishment from Cadmeko (Centre d'achat et de distribution des médicaments du Kasaï Oriental) and the Diulu health zone, following advocacy by the provincial Health Minister and the Justice Minister. Central government subsidy has been scarce, with only one disbursement at 70% since the start of the year, leaving debts and prompting appeals for assistance to meet prisoners' needs. No other diseases or outbreaks are detailed.

triage.headline_ja: カサイ・オリエンタル州：ムブジマイ中央刑務所で結核54例が報告
triage.triage_reason: 刑務所内という限定的な集団感染で国際的拡大の可能性は低いが、過密環境と医薬品不足により長期化・管理困難が懸念されるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 刑務所内の過密状態による結核集団感染。マラリア薬や他の医薬品不足も指摘されており、地方保健当局・司法省が支援を要請している。国際的拡大リスクは低いが、資源不足による管理困難が続く可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri: more than 60% case fatality rate due to the Ebola outbreak in Nia-Nia - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Nia-Nia health zone, Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeast Democratic Republic of Congo. As of August 7, 2026, 119 confirmed cases, 72 deaths and 24 recoveries reported, yielding a case fatality rate above 60%. The high lethality is linked to difficulties performing post-mortem sampling in PK51, with security constraints hampering response activities. About 90% of post-mortem samples tested in the area are positive, indicating intense community transmission. Response efforts remain limited due to major security constraints. Dr. Joseph Pemanakue, chief medical officer of the health zone, stressed the urgency of accelerating a full resumption of health interventions in PK51 to reduce mortality and interrupt the transmission chain. The report highlights ongoing Ebola transmission and the critical gaps in outbreak response caused by security and access challenges in PK51.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州:ニアニアでのエボラ流行、致死率60%超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の確定症例119名・死亡72名（致死率60%超）と重篤な公衆衛生上の脅威があり、治安上の制約により対応が困難で国際的拡大リスクも懸念されるためIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: PK51地域での治安上の制約により死後検体採取が困難であり、地域内感染が強く疑われる（陽性率約90%）。対応能力の限界が示唆されており、外部支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Main News of the Day | Friday: Ukraine, Gaza, Ebola, Food Prices
article.articleSummary: Ervebo vaccine is prioritized for clinical trials in the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC); Ervebo is the only registered Ebola vaccine, with demonstrated protection against Zaire ebolavirus, while efficacy against Bundibugyo ebolavirus circulating in the DRC remains to be proven. Separately, UN agencies report continued humanitarian activity amid conflict in Ukraine, with attacks on civilians causing casualties and injuries; Save the Children’s Sumy office was damaged, and two staff were wounded in Kherson, though aid delivery persists. In Gaza, July aid volumes rose 33% versus June, but imports remain restricted for certain cargo, including engine oil and spare parts, and building materials; the number of destroyed buildings in Gaza has increased by 9% since the ceasefire. Global food prices rose in July per FAO, driven by heat, energy costs, and Black Sea export disruptions, with wheat up 5.8%.

triage.headline_ja: 国連ニュース今日の主なニュース｜金曜日：ウクライナ、ガザ、エボラ、食料価格
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクにおいて、Bundibugyoエボラウイルスに対するワクチン（Ervebo）の有効性が未確認のまま臨床試験が優先されている点は、公衆衛生上の懸念及び国際的支援の必要性を示唆する。
triage.notes: 記事は国連の日次ニュースダイジェストの一部で、エボラに関する情報は簡潔。DRCで流行中のBundibugyoエボラウイルスに対するErveboワクチンの有効性が未証明のまま臨床試験が優先されている点が新規情報として注目される。ウクライナ・ガザは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: EU Authorizes Mpox Vaccine for Toddlers, Closing Deadly Gap for DRC Children
article.articleSummary: European Commission approves Bavarian Nordic's IMVANEX mpox/smallpox vaccine for children aged 2–11, the first major regulatory clearance of a non-replicating mpox vaccine for this age group, addressing a fatal gap in DRC where children under 15 represent about 60% of mpox cases and roughly 80% of deaths (UNICEF, 2024). The decision, adopted Aug 7, 2026, follows EMA/CHMP positive opinion (June 22–25, 2026) and extends EU authorization to ages two and up; the vaccine is marketed as IMVANEX in the EU and JYNNEOS in the US. A Phase 2 trial in the DRC and Uganda (NCT06549530) enrolled 227 children 2–11 and 224 adults; two doses 4 weeks apart; two weeks after dose 2, pediatric responses were non-inferior and 2.5× higher than adults, with safety similar to adults. MVA-BN cannot replicate in human cells, a key safety feature. In Sept–Oct 2024, 265,000 doses arrived in the DRC, but campaigns mainly targeted adults due to authorization gaps.

triage.headline_ja: EUがトイザー（幼児）向けMpoxワクチンを承認、DRCの子どもたちの致死的ギャップを解消
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はEUによるワクチン承認という規制上のニュースであり、新規の感染症発生や急激な状況変化を報告するものではないため、フルRRAへのシグナルとしては該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事はEUのMpoxワクチン（IMVANEX/JYNNEOS）の小児適応拡大承認に関するもので、DRCにおける既存の小児死亡率の高さを背景情報として言及している。新規アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、既知の状況への対応策（ワクチン供給改善）に関するニュース。

article.articleHeadline: Outbreak intensified during the monsoon: TB operations will be handed over to the Microbiology Department, the team conducted an investigation.
article.articleSummary: Monsoon-driven surge at Junagadh GMERS General Hospital saw 201 patients admitted to the Medicine department, with more than 25 new cases during the season. Infections include viral fever, dengue, malaria, and gastroenteritis. A high-level review by the medical superintendent, senior physician, and nursing in-charge examined ward operations, drug and fluid stocks, and treatment protocols, while proposing patient-care aids such as a suggestion box, QR codes, and diet-care passes to improve responsiveness. Emphasis was placed on infection control and sanitation. The hospital announced that TB department operations will be transferred to the Microbiology department, with the local team conducting an investigation into this transition as part of the intensified outbreak response during the monsoon.

triage.headline_ja: モンスーン中にアウトブレイクが激化：結核業務が微生物学部門に移管、チームが調査を実施
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のモンスーン期における通常の感染症増加（デング、マラリア、胃腸炎等）と病院内の組織再編に関する記事であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 地域の一病院における季節性感染症患者数の増加と院内業務再編に関するローカルニュースであり、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria data have raised concerns: In Bastar, more than 15,000 cases have been reported so far this year.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Bastar division, Chhattisgarh, has risen to over 15,000 confirmed cases in 2026 to date. After substantial reductions since 2015, annual positives climbed from 4,496 (2024) to 16,544 (2025) and 15,934 (2026 to date). From 2020–2026, testing remains high: 2022 saw 16,066 positives from 53,77,667 tests. The current year’s burden is highest in Bijapur, Sukma and Dantewada, with all seven Bastar districts affected; dense forests and remote villages delay access to health facilities. Since 2020, malaria deaths in the region total 127, distributed as Bastar 30, Kanker 7, Kondagaon 17, Narayanpur 4, Sukma 21, Dantewada 28, Bijapur 20. Mixed infections with Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax are increasingly reported, with P. vivax reinfection risk. Health officials urge prompt care at health centers as the 14th phase of Malaria-Free Bastar campaign continues.

triage.headline_ja: マラリアのデータが懸念を引き起こす：バスタルでは今年これまでに15,000件以上の症例が報告されている
triage.triage_reason: インド・チャッティースガル州バスタル地方における既知の風土病マラリアの年次症例報告であり、国際的拡大リスクは低いが、症例数増加（2024年4,496件→2025年16,544件→2026年15,934件）と死亡例の継続的発生から今後の推移を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事はインド・チャッティースガル州バスタル管区の地方風土病マラリアに関する年次統計報告。バングラデシュ（Khulna Division）は発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及がなく、主題国はインドのみと判断した。国際的な緊急性は低いが、遠隔森林地帯でのアクセス困難と混合感染（P. falciparum/P. vivax）の増加が地域の公衆衛生上の課題として指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Study links high PM2.5 exposure to increased risk of death among tuberculosis patients during treatment
article.articleSummary: 61,925 tuberculosis patients in Delhi who started treatment between September 2022 and August 2023 showed a strong link between pre-treatment PM2.5 exposure and mortality during therapy. Risk rose with increasing pollution in the month before treatment: 3% higher mortality for 40–80 µg/m³ vs <40; and 22%, 31%, and 66% higher for 80–120, 120–160, and >160 µg/m³, respectively. Researchers linked national Nikshay TB treatment records with satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates and focused on a 30-day pre-treatment window. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV, diabetes, nutritional status, tobacco/alcohol use, treatment setting, and TB type, the association persisted, though the study remains observational and cannot prove causality. This finding highlights India’s TB burden and suggests air pollution may influence TB outcomes; authors call for reducing exposure where possible and for further research to confirm mechanisms and potential clinical implications.

triage.headline_ja: 高いPM2.5曝露が結核患者の治療中死亡リスク増加と関連
triage.triage_reason: 大気汚染とTB治療死亡率の関連を示す観察研究であり、新興感染症の急性発生や公衆衛生上の異常事態ではないため、シグナルトリアージの対象外と判断。
triage.notes: 本研究は環境要因(PM2.5)と既知の慢性感染症(結核)の治療転帰の関連を示す疫学研究であり、新規発生・アウトブレイクではないためEBSトリアージの対象外。

article.articleHeadline: Exclusive: Eastern, Central States Lead India's Malaria Burden; Small States Among Least Affected
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains India's top vector-borne threat, concentrated in five states—West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Tripura—over 2023–2025, with Lakshadweep, Sikkim, Ladakh, Manipur and Puducherry among the least affected. West Bengal recorded 23,428 (2023), 19,497 (2024) and 18,872 (2025), with seasonal peaks in Sept 2023 (6,094), Sept 2024 (5,510) and Aug 2025 (4,020). Across India, 142 malaria deaths occurred in the period, led by Maharashtra (56), Mizoram (17), Odisha (14), Kerala (10) and Chhattisgarh (9). Odisha posted 32,064 (2023), 56,330 (2024) and 37,665 (2025) with top monthly burdens in Aug 2023 (8,016), July 2024 (14,293) and June 2025 (11,916). Jharkhand: 29,014; 32,533; 31,035 (peaks June 2023 11,405; Sept 2024 5,264; Aug 2025 4,804). Chhattisgarh: 19,461; 24,887; 18,497 (peaks July 2023 4,047; July 2024 5,525; June 2025 4,374). Tripura: 18,048; 6,924; 4,552 (peaks July 2023 4,837; June 2024 2,741; June 2025 1,913).

triage.headline_ja: 独占：インド東部・中部の州がマラリア負担で上位、小規模州は感染が少ない部類
triage.triage_reason: インドにおけるマラリアの季節的・恒常的な流行状況を報告する統計記事であり、異常な増加や新規の公衆衛生上の脅威を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 2023〜2025年の年次・季節的マラリア発生動向をまとめた統計報告記事。既知の風土病状況であり、突発的な異常事態ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Medical officers trained on Ebola, zoonoses in Dimapur
article.articleSummary: Medical Officers in Dimapur district participated in a capacity-building training on Ebola Virus Disease and zoonoses held at the CMO's Conference Hall on August 7, 2026. The Ebola segment, led by Dr. Ito T. Yeptho, covered epidemiology, transmission modes, clinical features, infection prevention and control, case definitions and reporting protocols, stressing early detection, safe specimen collection, and coordination with district surveillance for rapid response. Dr. K. Pewezo Khalo outlined protocols for collecting, transporting, testing, and submitting samples from suspected Ebola cases through the District Hospital laboratory network. The zoonoses session, led by Dr. Molungtsungba of IDSP, highlighted animal-to-human transmission routes and the One Health approach, with topics including rabies, anthrax, leptospirosis, and other locally relevant diseases, and the need for intersectoral coordination among health, animal husbandry, and community stakeholders. The training aimed to refresh guidelines under IDSP and strengthen diagnostic suspicion and reporting.

triage.headline_ja: ディマプールでエボラ・人獣共通感染症に関する医療従事者研修を実施
triage.triage_reason: 実際の感染症発生ではなく、医療従事者向けのエボラ・人獣共通感染症に関する研修イベントの報告であり、公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は疾病発生ではなく、インド・ナガランド州ディマプールで実施された医療従事者向けの能力構築研修（エボラ、狂犬病、炭疽、レプトスピラ症等の人獣共通感染症に関する）についての報告。実際の症例発生は言及されていない。

article.articleHeadline: International experts discuss emerging infectious disease threats at SRMIST
article.articleSummary: SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre (SRMIST) hosted the second international conference on Emerging and Re-emerging Infectious Diseases at SRMIST, attracting more than 400 delegates, including about 200 students, researchers, and early-career investigators, with roughly 30 national and international speakers. Over two days, sessions addressed pandemic preparedness, HIV pathogenesis, and the broader challenges of emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases. The event underscored the role of interdisciplinary research and durable international partnerships in strengthening global disease preparedness. Key speakers included S.P. Thyagarajan, former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Madras, who urged an integrated approach to combat emerging infections, and Rafick Sekaly, Vice-Chair of Translational Medicine at Emory University, who stressed nurturing the next generation of researchers. SRMIST Dean Sunil Narayan and Dean R. Jayanthi also spoke, highlighting scientific engagement and ongoing efforts at the institution.

article.articleHeadline: Agra News: Neither mouthpieces nor calibration are being changed; in the name of checking, infections are being spread.
article.articleSummary: Agra, India reports gaps in infection control during the Drink-and-Drive campaign using breath analyzers at dusk at key intersections (God Temple cinema area, Delhi Gate, MG Road). Although officials claim mouthpieces are changed after every test, inspections show reuse of mouthpieces, risking spread of bacteria and viruses. About 50 upgraded breath analyzers were recently supplied; disposable mouthpieces arrived, but several locations still reuse older pieces. On an average day, over 100 drivers test positive for alcohol; penalties under the Motor Vehicles Act apply for levels above the limit. Some officers wipe or clean mouthpieces and reuse them; health experts say disposable mouthpieces must be single-use. Rules require a separate mouthpiece per person, proper device preparation, mandatory change after each use, and periodic calibration. False positives can occur due to mouthwash, medicines, or food, prompting re-testing. Diseases of concern include influenza, TB, and COVID. Dr. Vinay Goel and Sonam Kumar comment on enforcement.

article.articleHeadline: The number of influenza patients is rising rapidly, with complaints that insurance is not being approved.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, Kerala, including Kochi, reports a sharp rise in influenza cases, with confirmed H1N1 infections. Insurance denials complicate care as New India Assurance policies reportedly refuse coverage for inpatient treatment, alleging hospitals bill for medical and ancillary charges beyond policy terms. Hospitals defend billing practices, while patients face mounting out-of-pocket costs. In one case, Bushir tested positive for H1N1 and, with two accompanying children, was admitted for eight and six days respectively, including two days in isolation; upon discharge, the insurer rejected the daughter’s entire bill. In another case, Meera, 65, and her five-year-old daughter, also diagnosed with H1N1, faced denial of Meera’s Rs 31,000 bill, with insurers citing insufficient documentation though hospital notes suggested inpatient care was unnecessary. The episode highlights an ongoing outbreak and financial hardship for affected families.

article.articleHeadline: The Scariest Thing About Influenza
article.articleSummary: Influenza can cause severe illness in Vietnamese children, not only those with underlying conditions. Dr. Pham Cong Khac of Bach Mai Hospital notes most children recover within a week with proper care, but flu can lead to pneumonia, dehydration, and in severe cases respiratory failure, myocarditis, encephalitis, seizures, rhabdomyolysis, shock, or multiorgan failure requiring ICU. High-risk groups include children under 5, especially under 2, with congenital heart disease, asthma, chronic lung disease, neurological or metabolic disorders, immune suppression, cancer, or on immunosuppressants; but healthy children can also worsen. Seek care for warning signs: difficulty or rapid breathing, blue lips, lethargy, seizures, poor feeding, dehydration, or prolonged fever. Vaccination remains the best preventive measure. In Vietnam, flu circulates year-round and peaks with weather changes; vaccines are updated annually, immunity takes about two weeks, and some children need two doses. Complementary measures: hand hygiene, masking, avoiding sick contacts, good ventilation, rest, fluids, nutrition; avoid unnecessary antibiotics.

article.articleHeadline: Guidelines for preventing gastrointestinal diseases and poisoning from drinking water sources.
article.articleSummary: Unsafe drinking water in Vietnam elevates the risk of acute gastrointestinal diseases—diarrhea, dysentery, typhoid—and food poisoning from microbial contamination (E. coli, Salmonella, Vibrio cholerae), with possible viral and parasitic infections. Long-term exposure to heavy metals (arsenic, lead, mercury, cadmium) and pesticides can accumulate, causing liver and kidney damage, neurodevelopment issues in children, and increased cancer risk. The Ministry of Health’s QCVN 01-1:2024/BYT sets 85 technical indicators across five groups for domestic water quality: microbiological (no E. coli or total coliform in 100 mL); physico-chemical (pH 6.0–8.5, turbidity ≤ 2 NTU, residual chlorine ≥ 0.2 mg/L at point of use); inorganic chemicals (e.g., arsenic ≤ 0.01 mg/L, lead ≤ 0.01 mg/L, nitrate ≤ 50 mg/L); organic pesticides (17 indicators); and radiological (α ≤ 0.1 Bq/L, β ≤ 1.0 Bq/L). Preventive measures include boiling, sealed storage, certified filtration (RO, Nano, UF) meeting QCVN for drinking water, regular tank cleaning (3–6 months), annual testing at provincial CDC labs, and protecting water sources.

article.articleHeadline: Hanoi records a case of whooping cough this summer.
article.articleSummary: 10 whooping cough cases were recorded by Hanoi CDC in the last three weeks of July, bringing the year-to-date total to 87—about 20 more than the same period previously. Bordetella pertussis infection causes respiratory illness and spreads by droplets and contact with contaminated objects. Early symptoms resemble a cold—fatigue, nasal congestion, runny nose, mild fever—before paroxysmal coughing with potential red face, post-tussive vomiting, and noisy breathing; infants may have poor feeding, cyanosis, apnea, pneumonia, seizures, or respiratory failure. Cases are year-round but pertussis typically peaks in winter–spring; seasonal transitions and incomplete vaccination may raise risk in the summer–autumn period. Prevention centers on full vaccination with boosters (ages 4–6, 9–15, every 10 years) and maternal Tdap during the third trimester. Vietnam uses vaccines containing pertussis components (5-in-1, 6-in-1, 4-in-1, 3-in-1); household vaccination and hygiene are advised.

article.articleHeadline: Military doctor advises on how to recognize and prevent COVID-19 in the face of new variants.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-07, rising Covid-19 cases across Vietnam are linked to SARS-CoV-2 variants NB.1.8.1, XFG.1.1, and BA.3.2 (Omicron), nicknamed the cicada variant. BA.3.2 is highly transmissible; current data show no evidence of greater severity than prior Omicron strains, though immune evasion may cause reinfection in those previously infected or vaccinated. Early signs include sore throat and hoarseness; other symptoms include fever, cough, fatigue, headache, nasal congestion, loss of smell or taste, and sometimes nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Covid-19 is a multi-system disease; lungs are most affected, but heart, liver, and kidneys can be involved. High-risk groups—elderly, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, immunodeficiency, chronic lung disease—require closer monitoring. Preventive measures: vaccination, hand hygiene, masking in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces. Seek medical care for severe symptoms; avoid self-medication with antivirals or antibiotics.

article.articleHeadline: Diagnosed with hepatitis B and then stopped treatment for 20 years, a 53-year-old man needs dialysis; his wife and children are also infected.
article.articleSummary: 53-year-old man from Nam Định Province discovered hepatitis B 20 years ago; after antiviral therapy he felt well and stopped follow-up, assuming clearance. HBV can persist silently in liver cells for decades, gradually causing inflammation, fibrosis, cirrhosis, ascites, esophageal variceal bleeding, and eventual liver failure or cancer, often with no early signs. Twenty years later he presents with fatigue, abdominal distension, and infection-related complications, now dialysis-dependent. His wife and children were not tested or vaccinated until screening revealed infection. In another Nam Định family, two brothers inherited HBV from their mother; the elder was diagnosed early and adheres to treatment and prevention for his wife and children, while the younger, diagnosed at 45, also transmits to wife and son. After treatment at Bach Mai Institute of Tropical Diseases and Bach Mai Hospital, health improved. Emphasizes routine viral-load testing, fibrosis assessment, vaccination, and not stopping antivirals without medical guidance; mother-to-child transmission remains a key route.

article.articleHeadline: Prolonged fever after COVID-19: a 43-year-old man diagnosed with rare tuberculous pericarditis.
article.articleSummary: 43-year-old man in Ho Chi Minh City presented with fever after COVID-19, tachycardia to 170 bpm, and dyspnea. Echocardiography showed pericardial effusion with concurrent pleural effusion. Pericardiocentesis and pleural drainage were performed; CT chest/abdomen was nondiagnostic. Pericardial fluid analysis detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis, diagnosing tuberculous pericarditis, a rare extrapulmonary TB form (~1% of TB). The infection can compress the heart, reduce pumping, cause heart failure, and threaten life if untreated. The patient likely experienced latent TB reactivation after COVID-19–related immune decline. He began standard anti-tuberculosis therapy; after about two weeks fever and dyspnea improved markedly. After roughly 20 days, he was afebrile and discharged, continuing TB therapy for at least 6 months. Early detection and full adherence yield favorable prognosis; vaccination with BCG and latent TB screening are advised for high-risk groups.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo calls for a stronger response and international solidarity, according to Africa CDC.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Bundibugyo strain) worsens; since the outbreak was declared on May 15, 2026, the DRC has 3,973 confirmed cases and 1,801 deaths (case fatality >45%), with about 776 recoveries. The 17th outbreak has expanded from 9 to 51 health zones affected. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya called for stronger international support to close critical response gaps and for studies on possible viral mutation. Major obstacles include limited contact-tracing capacity, rising community transmission, insufficient hospital beds, funding shortages, insecurity, and unsafe burials. Uganda is praised for interrupting local transmission, while 11 other African countries are deemed high-risk: South Sudan, Rwanda, Kenya, Zambia, Central African Republic, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Angola, Republic of the Congo, Burundi and Somalia.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak: Africa rolls out vaccines and expands treatment.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) worsens as Africa CDC (ACDC) on August 6 expands vaccination with the Ebola Zaire vaccine in Ituri and North Kivu to reduce mortality amid the Bundibugyo driven surge. Vaccinated individuals can still contract Ebola, but no deaths have been recorded among them. ACDC also expands remdesivir use for treatment, drawing on Uganda’s experience where mortality was about 10 percent and the outbreak ended in mid July after the last patient discharge. The DRC Health Ministry tallies 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths; 793 recovered and 694 still in treatment or isolation. MSF warns the outbreak is spreading rapidly, with 60 to 70 percent of new cases outside monitored lists, expanding to 51 health zones from 9. Kinshasa has reported no confirmed cases, though about 200 passengers on a near Kinshasa ship were quarantined after a traveler died with suspected Ebola symptoms. Eleven other African countries are at high risk: South Sudan, Rwanda, Kenya, Zambia, Central African Republic, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Angola, Republic of Congo, Burundi, Somalia.

article.articleHeadline: Don't wade through standing water after rain; standing water harbors pathogens and can cause various diseases, warns the National CDC.
article.articleSummary: Following persistent rainfall, urban waterlogging has become severe in some Chinese cities. People are wading through floodwater for convenience. The National CDC warns that floodwater in cities can damage sewer and wastewater systems and mix with bacteria, viruses, and parasites, creating a reservoir of pathogens in standing water combined with sewage, silt, and garbage. Skin contact or exposure through broken skin to polluted floodwater can trigger skin infections, dermatitis, and gastrointestinal (enteric) infections. Stagnant water also fosters mosquitoes, increasing the risk of vector-borne diseases. During rain, avoid wading through water; if you must, minimize skin exposure and time spent in water. After returning home, thoroughly rinse and wash skin that has been in floodwater and keep skin clean and dry.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: US maintains travel ban on Uganda
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, the United States maintains a Level 4 Do Not Travel advisory for Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and South Sudan, despite Africa CDC and WHO urging reconsideration of Uganda travel limits. The State Department says the priority is protecting Americans and containing Ebola at the source. Uganda’s Ebola outbreak, announced May 15 and linked to DR Congo transmission, produced 20 cases, 2 deaths, and 18 recoveries; 15 cases were imported from DR Congo. Uganda declared the outbreak over on 28 July after discharging the last patient on 16 June. The United States announced an additional $242 million for Ebola response (total direct Ebola funding now $512 million) plus $350 million in humanitarian aid; China’s contributions are described as under 1% of US support. Uganda’s health minister urged lifting restrictions to aid the economy; WHO Africa regional director Prof. Mohamed Yakub Janabi congratulated Uganda on outbreak control. Response activated within 24–48 hours of first reports.

article.articleHeadline: FEHD: Aedes albopictus (white-striped mosquito) widely distributed in the monitored area but not numerous; has intensified mosquito-control efforts (16:54) - 2026-08-07.
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong’s Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) reports Aedes albopictus, the white-striped mosquito, is widely distributed in the monitored area but not numerous. In the past month, FEHD conducted over 69,000 inspections, initiated 17 prosecutions for mosquito breeding, and issued 69 statutory notices to remove standing water or containers. The third phase of the citywide anti-mosquito campaign began on July 3 and runs through October 23, targeting homes, schools, construction sites, and public housing estates to eliminate breeding sites and apply ultra-low-volume mist to kill adult mosquitoes in high-risk areas. To reduce chikungunya transmission, FEHD will expand intensified control from a 20% trap-index threshold to include areas with 10–20% indices, performing risk assessments and coordinating with departments and stakeholders. Vector surveillance and targeted control will also be conducted within 250 meters of residences of chikungunya and dengue patients and at locations visited during the infection period.

article.articleHeadline: Parasites have taken up residence in the spinal cord for 12 years, leaving a 55-year-old man with hemiplegia
article.articleSummary: A 55-year-old man from Hunan, China, with a 12-year history of spinal sparganosis due to sparganum larvae of Spirometra mansoni presented with progressive neurological decline, including dizziness, occipital pain, vomiting, urinary difficulty, back pain, bilateral leg numbness/weakness, and right eye atrophy. Thoracolumbar MRI showed long-segment intradural lesions compressing the thoracic–lumbar cord and cauda equina. A multidisciplinary team at Southern Medical University Third Affiliated Hospital diagnosed spinal sparganosis, prompted by exposure history (lake-adjacent living; consumption of fish, bullfrogs, and eels; potential ingestion of undercooked meat or contaminated water, and use of frog meat on wounds/eyes). On July 23, decompression, lesion clearance, adhesiolysis, and lamina reconstruction were performed; intraoperative inspection found no live worms, but white material from parasitic activity remained. Postoperative pathology and molecular testing confirmed Spirometra mansoni sparganum. Leg strength improved from grade 2 to 3. Prevention emphasizes avoiding undercooked frog/fish meat, contaminated water, and cross-contamination. A similar 2024 case was treated at this hospital.

article.articleHeadline: The coronavirus mystery returns: New questions about the origin of the virus!
article.articleSummary: Renewed questions about the origin of the coronavirus—whether COVID-19 arose naturally or resulted from a laboratory-related incident—dominate analysis as of August 7, 2026. The White House now endorses the lab-leak hypothesis, portraying it as the origin after years of ambiguity. Critics question why the theory is resurfacing now and why intelligence agencies did not take a definitive position earlier. The report notes that the updated White House page on COVID-19 origins does not present new scientific findings but reiterates conclusions from the 2024 Congressional committee’s final report, which favored a lab-related accident in Wuhan, China as a plausible origin, supported by several arguments. No new laboratory-confirmation data is reported. Details are linked in an accompanying video.

article.articleHeadline: Shandong Province Kick-off Meeting for the Sino-Guinea Tuberculosis Prevention and Control Cooperation Project Held in Qingdao
article.articleSummary: On August 7, in Jimo District, Qingdao, Shandong Province, the Sino-Guinea Tuberculosis Prevention and Control Cooperation Project launched its Shandong phase. The initiative aims to strengthen close-contact screening and comprehensive hospital patient detection research in low-incidence TB areas, as part of the China–Guinea TB collaboration between the National Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the Gates Foundation. Since its 2009 start, the program has advanced TB diagnostic tool validation and patient-management models. China’s TB situation is improving but remains challenging, with regional disparities and gaps in prevention. The Shandong launch supports the national TB-control plan and the 2025–2030 Shandong TB Plan, targeting an incidence below 18 per 100,000 by 2030. The project emphasizes contact tracing, preventive therapy, proactive patient discovery, and knowledge synthesis to inform policy and create a replicable, scalable model for nationwide use and international collaboration.

article.articleHeadline: China Reports Four More H9N2 Infections as U.S. Bird Flu Risk Stays Low for the General Public
article.articleSummary: On 7 August 2026, the World Health Organization reported four additional human infections with avian influenza A(H9N2) in China during July 24–30: a 72-year-old woman in Jiangxi, a 12-year-old boy in Jiangsu, a 3-year-old girl in Gansu, and a 58-year-old woman in Yunnan. One case had direct live-poultry exposure; three were linked to live-poultry stalls or wet markets. Two hospitalized patients with chronic respiratory conditions were discharged; the other two had mild illness and recovered. U.S. public risk remains low, while workers with prolonged animal contact face greater risk and are advised to use protective equipment. Since 2015, 164 Western Pacific Region H9N2 cases with two deaths; 2026 may meet or exceed last year’s total. In six months, 20 known global infections (12 in China; 1 each in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Italy). H5N1 is high-pathogenic, with 12 external infections and three deaths; no sustained human transmission. Precautions include PPE for at‑risk workers and household measures: avoid sick/dead wild birds; cook poultry and eggs; avoid raw milk.

article.articleHeadline: Safety Guidelines for Hazards of Internal Parasites in Cats and Their Prevention and Control.
article.articleSummary: China-based feline internal-parasite control emphasizes exposure-risk assessment and the cat’s health status before selecting a compliant oral dewormer. For ordinary healthy cats needing coverage of nine internal parasites and heartworm larvae, Pu’an Te Pu Le Miao (milbemycin oxime + praziquantel) oral tablets provide dual nematode and cestode protection plus heartworm larva prevention. Third-party data show active ingredients within 90–110% of labeled amounts and bioequivalence to standard milbemycin oxime–praziquantel products. The formulation targets roundworms and hookworms, several cestodes (including Dipylidium caninum), and heartworm larvae, but does not address external parasites or protozoa, requiring additional products for fleas, mites, Giardia, Coccidia, or Tritrichomonas. High-risk cats—6 weeks or younger, under 0.5 kg, pregnant/lactating, ill, or with liver/kidney disease or prior dewormer reactions—must be veterinarian-evaluated before use. Dosing is weight-based; routine intestinal protection is every 3 months, with annual fecal parasite testing recommended.

article.articleHeadline: Brain-Eating Worm (Angiostrongylus cantonensis): Thai Man's Binge on Raw, Brined Seafood Causes Severe Intestinal Ulceration, Recurrent Massive Bleeding and Shock, Nearly Died
article.articleSummary: One Shanghai man, Xu (pseudonym), contracted Entamoeba histolytica after extensive consumption of raw and brined seafood during a business trip to Thailand. Upon return, he developed fulminant amebic enteritis with widespread intestinal ulcers, recurrent massive bleeding, and septic shock. Despite multiple surgeries, he remained critically ill, with severe inflammation, coagulation dysfunction, and hemoglobin dropping below 6 g/dL, risking intestinal perforation and death. He was transferred to Shanghai Public Health Clinical Center for emergency care, where a personalized, multidisciplinary treatment plan over more than 30 days controlled bleeding and infection, ultimately achieving survival. Entamoeba histolytica infections are common in tropical/subtropical regions; foodborne exposure through raw seafood is a notable risk. Travelers are advised to enforce strict food and water hygiene and seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, or vomiting, especially in hot weather. The report also notes parasitic risks associated with seafood consumption.

article.articleHeadline: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and the shifting epicenter of pulmonary tuberculosis notifications in thailand over a 10-year period: Evidence from national surveillance data
article.articleSummary: Pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) in Thailand shows marked spatiotemporal heterogeneity from 2014–2023, despite a national decline in incidence. Global Moran's I found no significant nationwide clustering, but Local Indicators of Spatial Association revealed evolving local hotspots. Space-time scan statistics detected seven clusters; the most likely cluster shifted from the Eastern industrial region (2014–2019; RR=3.64; LLRatio=1,463.28) to the Lower Northeastern border region (2020–2023; including Ubon Ratchathani, Si Sa Ket, Amnat Charoen, Yasothon, Roi Et; RR=3.22; LLRatio=3,145.62; P<0.001). Notification completeness affected interpretation: 154 of 770 province-years (20%) had zero notified cases, concentrated 2014–2016. The Eastern cluster had annual notifications, while many Lower Northeastern and Prachuap Khiri Khan province-years were zero in 2014–2016. The shift likely reflects reporting changes, not transmission; highlights the need to assess reporting completeness before space-time analyses and supports geographically targeted improvements in TB surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: PhilHealth offers leptospirosis benefit package

The Department of Health warned the public about leptospirosis risk on Aug 6, 2026, as torrential rains continue. DOH had recorded 2,877 leptospirosis cases nationwide as of July 18. The initiative aims to assist flood-hit individuals at risk and emphasizes timely action when wading through floodwaters; do not neglect health.

article.articleHeadline: Zamboanga mayor wants more fogging machines as dengue deaths hit 12

article.articleHeadline: Over 17,000 bats documented in JAS
article.articleSummary: DENR-Davao Region documented over 17,000 island flying foxes (Pteropus hypomelanus) and large flying foxes (Pteropus vampyrus) in Jose Abad Santos, Davao Occidental, during the 2026 Monitoring of Threatened Species conducted in Barangay Bukid on Aug 4, 2026. Using the exit count method, observers estimated populations and roost locations by tallying bats as they emerged at dusk for about 30 minutes. Beyond Jose Abad Santos, large flying foxes are also found on Luban Island, Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary, and Mount Apo Natural Park. Flying foxes, protected under Republic Act No. 9147, play key ecological roles as pollinators, seed dispersers, and natural pest controllers, yet remain threatened and are recognized natural reservoirs for Nipah virus. The island flying fox is the smallest member of the group, typically roosting on offshore islands in coconut palms and tall trees. The Philippines hosts about 70 bat species, among ~1,400 worldwide.

article.articleHeadline: Monkayo under heightened alert due to ASF
article.articleSummary: Monkayo, a municipality in Davao de Oro, Philippines, is under heightened alert due to an alleged African Swine Fever (ASF) outbreak. The Philippines’ ASF outbreak began in July 2019; as of July 10, 2026, active ASF cases were recorded in 21 barangays across 17 cities/municipalities in 11 provinces. In support, Davao de Oro inaugurated a P10-million Swine Multiplier and Technology Demonstration Farm under the INSPIRE Program to rehabilitate the hog industry after ASF. The Health Office continues to provide medical consultations, injury treatment, water/sanitation monitoring, nutrition services, and mental health support in evacuation centers during floods.

article.articleHeadline: Public health alert in Santa Cruz over a suspected measles case: which symptoms should be monitored.
article.articleSummary: Suspected measles case in Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, has prompted a health alert as authorities activate the preventive protocol per national guidelines. The Expanded Immunization Program and Hospital Zonal Epidemiology units urge vaccination with MMR. Measles is highly contagious and can cause pneumonia, encephalitis, or hearing loss; it spreads via airborne droplets and contaminated surfaces and can remain viable for up to two hours. An infected person can transmit to about 9 of 10 non-vaccinated contacts. Symptoms include high fever, red rash, cough, runny nose, conjunctivitis, and white Koplik spots inside the cheeks; severe cases may require hospitalization. First MMR dose at 12 months; second dose after the first year; adults born before 1965 are generally protected; health workers should be up-to-date. Travelers should verify vaccination before travel and seek care if symptoms appear.

article.articleHeadline: 93,155 dengue cases reported this year

article.articleHeadline: Rise in HIV Infections Raises Alarm Among Health Authorities.
article.articleSummary: Latin America shows rising HIV infections between 2010 and 2025, according to the UNAIDS Global Report 2026 published 2026-08-07, with Brazil noting higher incidence amid broader HIV treatment progress. The report highlights substantial advances in antiretroviral therapy and prevention, yet Latin America diverges from other continents where incidence declines. Prevention measures include pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP); when used correctly and with ongoing healthcare follow-up, these strategies markedly reduce infection risk. In Brazil, the Unified Health System (SUS) provides PrEP/PEP following clinical assessment. Testing remains central: sexually active individuals at higher risk are advised to test every three to six months and to seek care after a risk exposure. Brazil reported 38,222 new HIV infections in 2023 and 39,216 in 2024, underscoring ongoing transmission despite prevention efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Einstein study on viral hepatitis maps the disease landscape over eleven years.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from Einstein Hospital analyzed 200 studies (2013–2024) totaling data on over 14.5 million people to map viral hepatitis across Brazil. Part of the Proadi-SUS–backed project, the study aims to inform prevention and care to reach Brazil’s 2030 elimination goal for viral hepatitis, and was published in PLOS ONE. All five hepatitides A–E are covered. Hepatitis A is acute and vaccine‑preventable, with a resurgence linked to oral/anal sex among men who have sex with men and to fecal‑oral transmission via contaminated food/water; highest regional burden in the Amazon and the North/Northeast, with adults over 18 also affected in the South, Southeast, and Central‑West due to behavioral and vaccination gaps. Hepatitis B and C share sexual and blood‑borne routes; B can be chronic and is vaccine‑preventable, C lacks a vaccine but is highly curable (>95%). Hepatitis D is neglected, prevalent in Amazon riverine populations with diagnostic challenges, and often co‑circulates with B.

article.articleHeadline: Bovine rabies cases advance and put herds on alert - Ponta Porã Informs - News from Ponta Porã - Mato Grosso do Sul and Pedro Juan Caballero - Paraguay.
article.articleSummary: Rabies in herbivores is prompting alerts across southern Brazil. In early 2026, Paraná confirmed 75 cases (69 cattle, 6 horses) across 57 foci, including near Parque Nacional do Iguaçu. Santa Catarina registered 27 bovine cases this year, with circulation from the north to Itajaí Valley; Itapiranga is a recent location. In 2025, Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul reported 230 infected animals in 197 foci, over 80% cattle, prompting vaccination mandates in western Paraná. Rio Grande do Sul had 45 active foci by June across ten regions, with alerts in several municipalities. Outside the region, Bezerros, Pernambuco, reported a rabid horse in July, triggering vaccination in six nearby municipalities. Transmission is primarily via Desmodus rotundus; infected animals show neurological signs and usually die within days. Vaccination starts at three months, boosters after 30 days, annual revaccination; isolate symptomatic animals and report bat roosts; control by authorized teams.

triage.notes: コウモリ（Desmodus rotundus）由来の家畜狂犬病がブラジル南部（パラナ、サンタカタリーナ、リオグランデドスル）およびペルナンブコ州で拡大。ワクチン接種義務化などの対策が取られているが、ヒト感染例の報告はなく、公衆衛生上の緊急性は現時点で低い。

article.articleHeadline: Dental clinic is shut down in Belém due to risk of infection.
article.articleSummary: Belém, Pará, Brazil – A dental clinic in the Icoaraci district has been interdicted on a precautionary basis by the Municipal Health Secretariat (Sesma) after a sanitary inspection by the Department of Sanitary Surveillance (DEVISA) identified irregularities during licensing. Investigators found deficiencies in biosafety practices, infrastructure conditions, and cleaning, with irregularities in the processing and sterilization of dental instruments. The health authority warned that such failures could raise the risk of infection transmission among patients and staff, including serious viral diseases like hepatitis and HIV. The clinic had been notified earlier to obtain a sanitary license and implement required adaptations, but a subsequent inspection found no corrective actions. The temporary interdiction means the clinic cannot resume care until all irregularities are corrected and regularization with the sanitary surveillance authority is completed. Patients are advised to verify licensure, hygiene, and that sterilized instruments are properly sealed and opened in their presence.

article.articleHeadline: Dentist arrested after being accused of deliberately transmitting HIV to several women in Rondônia.
article.articleSummary: HIV exposure case in Rondônia, Brazil: A dentist in Porto Velho has been arrested after allegedly deliberately transmitting HIV to several women with whom he had relationships. The Ministério Público de Rondônia filed charges; the clinician knew of his HIV diagnosis for ten years and did not seek treatment to control the virus. The case came to light after three women diagnosed with HIV; a fourth victim has been identified during investigations. Authorities fear more individuals may have been exposed. The dentist is imprisoned and faces charges including rape, danger of contagion of a grave disease, and grievous bodily harm, with potential penalties totaling up to ten years in prison plus fines. Ongoing investigations may reveal additional victims.

article.articleHeadline: Araçatuba CCZ trains health teams and reinforces strategies for leishmaniasis prevention.
article.articleSummary: Araçatuba’s Centro de Controle de Zoonoses (CCZ) conducted a technical training on August 7, 2026, to strengthen leishmaniasis surveillance, prevention and control under the Week of Prevention and Control of Visceral Leishmaniasis. Led by veterinarian Andresa Xavier, the session updated the Manual of Leishmaniasis and aligned canine and human management with the latest Ministry of Health and State Health Secretariat guidelines for visceral leishmaniasis. Key topics covered diagnostic workflows for dogs, including biospecimen collection, rapid diagnostic test (DPP), confirmatory ELISA, result interpretation, and handling inconclusive cases. Emphasis on canine case management, responsible ownership, entomological surveillance and environmental control of the sand fly vector. Field practices: sanitary notification forms, domiciliary visit reports, active search for suspects, and early human case identification. From January–July 2026, two human cases (one fatal); 177 dogs tested positive, vs 286 canine cases in the same period last year.

triage.notes: リーシュマニア症はブラジルの一部地域で風土病化しており、本記事は定例の予防・サーベイランス強化活動を報じるもの。2026年1-7月に人での症例2件（うち1件死亡）が報告されているが、前年同期の犬の陽性数(286件)より今年(177件)は減少しており、拡大傾向は見られない。

article.articleHeadline: Check which neighborhood will receive dengue control services this Friday in Campo Grande.
article.articleSummary: On Friday, Campo Grande’s vector-control program by Sesau will spray only Bairro Nova Lima in the afternoon (16:00–22:00) to combat dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. The UBV Ultra Low Volume fumigation targets adult mosquitoes, especially females. Residents are urged to open doors and windows to maximize effectiveness. Operations by the CCEV (Coordenadoria de Controle de Endemias Vetoriais) may be delayed or canceled in case of rain, wind, or fog, which impair application. Although intended to reduce disease transmission, the insecticide can affect non-target species, requiring careful deployment. The article does not provide case or death counts, and focuses on ongoing weekly control activities in Campo Grande, with notification of the single-neighborhood schedule for the week.

article.articleHeadline: After five days locked up, the pit bull that attacked its owner in Mondubim is taken for rabies tests.
article.articleSummary: Rabies-related observations in Fortaleza, Brazil: A pit bull that attacked its owner in Mondubim was moved on August 6 for veterinary observation and rabies testing, coordinated by the Zoonoses Surveillance Unit (UVZ) under the Municipal Health Secretariat. The dog will remain under observation for about ten days, after which it is expected to be returned to its guardians, subject to public authorities' authorization. The owner remains hospitalized from injuries sustained in the weekend attack. The dog had reportedly been left alone for five days inside the residence without water or food. Leishmaniasis testing returned negative. SPA-CE indicated two guardians prepared to assume responsible custody, pending official assessment. The attack occurred on Saturday, August 1, at Travessa Jaboticaba, Mondubim; police and neighbors contained the animal and provided initial care to the victim.

article.articleHeadline: Test confirms Rocky Mountain spotted fever in a veterinarian who died in São Fidélis.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, São Fidélis, Rio de Janeiro, confirmed Rocky Mountain spotted fever in a veterinarian and entrepreneur who died last week. The final test for the deceased, Gabriel Serra, was positive; five other patients tested negative, and one person remains hospitalized. The disease is a severe tick-borne infection caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, transmitted mainly by the star tick, and is not contagious person-to-person. Key symptoms include high fever, headache, muscle pains, and skin rashes. Following confirmation, the municipality will continue integrated interventions led by the Municipal Health, Environmental Development, Agricultural Development, and Civil Defense departments, per health surveillance protocols. Authorities isolated the property entrance where the tick bite likely occurred. A team from the Rio de Janeiro State Health Secretariat also visited to monitor the response.

article.articleHeadline: Measles pockets do not respect ideology, says infectious-disease specialist.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreaks in São Paulo state, Brazil, comprise 23 confirmed cases as of August 7, 2026. The article warns that vaccination coverage is below ideal, creating space for the virus to circulate. Two doses of measles vaccine are required for full protection. Infectious-disease specialist Luana Araújo notes that pockets of unvaccinated individuals, not aligned with any ideology, reveal difficulties in understanding health information and communicating public-health messages. The report underscores the importance of improving vaccination uptake to curb transmission. No further details on lab confirmation, infection sources, or imported/exported cases are provided. Overall, the situation illustrates ongoing measles transmission risk in São Paulo due to suboptimal vaccine coverage.

triage.headline_ja: 麻疹の集団発生はイデオロギーとは無関係、感染症専門医が指摘
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・サンパウロ州で麻疹23例確認、ワクチン接種率低下による感染継続リスクが示唆されるが、重症度や拡大規模の詳細情報が不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はワクチン接種率低下と情報伝達の課題を指摘するが、症例の重症度や地理的拡大の詳細は不明。続報での感染者数推移やワクチン接種状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Brazil's experience with dengue fever will be applied in 'La Ciudad Bonita'.
article.articleSummary: Brazil's Fiocruz and the Universidad de Santander (UDES) shared Brazil's dengue strategy with Bucaramanga's metropolitan area, La Ciudad Bonita. The approach combines vaccination with clinical research and surveillance to reduce hospitalizations and strengthen dengue response. Researchers Rafaella Fortini Grenfell, Queiroz, and Priscilla Fernanda da Silva Martins noted two vaccines for ages 10–59 with about 80% efficacy, with ongoing evaluation of results. Fortini, an advisor to WHO, Brazil's Health Ministry, and ANVISA, stressed continuous assessment of outcomes. Given Colombia and Brazil circulate all four dengue serotypes, integrated vaccination, vector control, and elimination of Aedes aegypti breeding sites are essential. Fiocruz conducts phase IV studies to assess safety, immunogenicity, real-world effectiveness, and determine boosters and predominant serotypes. The exchange strengthens scientific cooperation and may incorporate international evidence into Santander's dengue strategies.

article.articleHeadline: Wild Boars in Brazil Are Spreading Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria, Scientists Warn
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-07, researchers screened 100 rectal swabs from European wild boars on two Goiás State farms for Salmonella and Escherichia coli, assessing antibiotic resistance and virulence genes. Salmonella was rare (1/100) and, though resistant to several antibiotics, lacked virulence and resistance markers, suggesting low immediate risk. E. coli was widespread: 56 isolates, with 55 (98.2%) multidrug resistant, notably to sulfonamides, tetracycline, amoxicillin, ampicillin, and doxycycline; nearly all remained susceptible to ceftriaxone. tsh appeared in ~30% of E. coli isolates; papC and iss were less common, with some strains carrying multiple virulence genes. The environment and One Health framework are emphasized: resistance genes persist in soil and water and can move between bacteria; wild boar mobility and farm interfaces may spread resistance. Researchers caution that samples (2014–2017) came from only two farms and antibiotic-use data were not independently verified; captive boars should enter health surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Avian influenza confirmed in a wild bird at Ibirapuera Park in São Paulo.
article.articleSummary: On August 7, 2026, the São Paulo state government confirmed a case of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in a wild bird found at Ibirapuera Park, in southern São Paulo. The species, Dendrocygna viduata (white-faced whistling duck), tested positive after lab confirmation following sampling by the Defesa Agropecuária. Authorities emphasize this is an isolated event in free-ranging wildlife and does not affect Brazil's or São Paulo's sanitary status with the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE). There is no impact on the poultry production chain, and consumption of poultry and eggs remains safe. A 10-km safety radius shows no commercial poultry facilities nearby. Ongoing epidemiological surveillance will monitor for clinical signs in other birds, and health teams are monitoring people who had contact with the infected bird. Coordination between PESA and animal protection agencies ensures continuous monitoring.

article.articleHeadline: Coahuila reinforces its strategy against the wood-boring worm; maintains 36 active cases.
article.articleSummary: Coahuila reports 36 active screwworm myiasis cases, concentrated in the Southeast (Saltillo, General Cepeda, Arteaga, Ramos Arizpe) with some in Centro and Norte. Eleven joint field brigades of federal and state agencies survey ranch lands to inspect animals, treat wounds with cicatrizants, and administer antiparasitics (ivermectin or doramectin) for about 30–60 days. About 25% of cases involve companion or backyard animals, including ranch dogs and urban pets. When wounds are found, animals are isolated and reported for sampling to confirm screwworm larvae versus other myiasis; larvae are removed and deeper wounds treated. Sterile-fly dispersal continues across regions including Centro, Norte, Don Martín dam, Progreso, Juárez, Carbonífera, Muzquiz, and border towns Zaragoza, Acuña, Piedras Negras, Guerrero, Hidalgo. A Chiapas plant will raise weekly sterile-fly production from ~20 million to 100–120 million by 2028. No animal deaths; recovery in 1–2 weeks with timely care.

article.articleHeadline: Genetic characterizations and seroprevalence of hepatitis B virus among non-human primates and human caretakers in Indonesia
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA is detected in Indonesian non-human primates (NHPs) and human caretakers across four islands, in an unedited study of 237 NHPs across 10 species and 65 human handlers. First detection of HBV DNA in the East Javan langur (Trachypithecus auratus) with 2/46 tested positives, plus serological exposure. HBV DNA is also detected in gibbons (17/68), orangutans (4/50), and humans (5/65), but not in macaques (0/73). Serology shows HBcAb and HBeAb positivity in the langur, and HBsAb positivity in six additional langurs (8/46 total) and in 6/68 macaques. HBsAb is found in gibbons (7/47) and orangutans (16/46). Phylogenetic analyses place the langur HBV strains within the gibbon HBV clade. Langur viral DNA levels are low and undetectable on resampling after six months in one case; findings warrant mechanistic follow-up and sustained primate-human interface surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: HIV Cases in North Penajam Paser Regency Rise
article.articleSummary: HIV/AIDS cases in North Penajam Paser Regency (PPU), East Kalimantan, rise in 2026, with 17 new HIV diagnoses by June and a total of 110 ODHIV (people living with HIV/AIDS) by July. Six of the June cases were deaths. Distribution by subdistrict: Penajam 64, Sepaku 26, Babulu 11, Waru 9. Officials attribute the uptick to expanded HIV testing and treatment access in Sepaku, not migrant inflows related to the IKN project. Service expansion since 2021–2025 includes Sepaku III, RSUD Pratama Sepaku, and three new facilities, enabling ART and viral load testing under Layanan Perawatan, Dukungan, dan Pengobatan (PDP). The key population driving growth is men who have sex with men (LSL); 7 LSL cases were recorded in June 2026. Age distribution: 92 of 110 cases are 20–40 years old. 11 Puskesmas and 2 government hospitals provide testing and PDP; private hospitals Hermina Nusantara and Mayapada Nusantara offer HIV testing but not PDP.

article.articleHeadline: Dangers of Exercising When Not Fit Can Worsen Systemic Infections.
article.articleSummary: Jakarta, Indonesia – August 7, 2026. Exercising while sick or not fully fit can raise the body's workload and slow recovery from infections, according to Dr. Tirta Mandira Hudhi, a physician and health influencer. In an Instagram video, he explains that when ill the immune system is already working hard and the body needs extra energy to recover. Pushing through illness, particularly with systemic infections, may prolong healing and increase the risk of complications affecting other organs. He cites heavier illnesses such as dengue fever, typhoid fever, diarrhea, and poisoning, noting that energy demands rise during systemic infections. The guidance emphasizes avoiding intense physical activity when the body is fighting infection to prevent extended illness or deterioration, a message targeted at the general public in Jakarta.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria resistance looms, drug efficacy nearly at a critical threshold.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Indonesia shows early signs of resistance to piperaquine, though artemisinin and its derivatives remain effective according to researchers. BRIN reports that some parasites can survive therapy, complicating distinctions between reinfection and treatment failure. Genetic markers pfpm2 and pfmdr1 are used to monitor resistance patterns, with initial data indicating most parasites remain theoretically sensitive to piperaquine, yet field isolates exhibit survival post-therapy. The finding suggests resistance mechanisms are more complex than anticipated and calls for deeper genetic studies. BRIN is also pursuing new molecular targets for next-generation antimalarials, notably the apicoplast, a parasite-specific organelle vital to metabolism. Researchers warn that Plasmodium will continue to evolve genetically, underscoring ongoing research to preserve current therapies and accelerate discovery of new drugs to support Indonesia's malaria elimination target by 2030.

triage.headline_ja: マラリア耐性が忍び寄る、薬剤効果は危機的閾値に迫る
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアでマラリア原虫の薬剤耐性の初期兆候が研究レベルで報告されているが、実際の臨床的耐性拡大や公衆衛生への深刻な影響は未確認であり、続報を注視すべき段階。
triage.notes: 研究段階の報告であり、実際の治療失敗例の規模や臨床的影響については記事内で明示されていない。BRINによる継続的なモニタリング研究の一環。
